summary.value: The Plymouth Rock is an American dual-purpose chicken from Massachusetts, first shown in the mid 1800s. Until about World War II it was the most common chicken on US farms. The first birds were barred, with crisp black and white stripes, and later colors include white, buff, blue, partridge and Columbian. It has a single red comb, yellow legs and yellow skin. Hens weigh around 7.5 pounds and roosters around 9.5. A hen lays roughly 200 large brown eggs a year, and the breed also gives a good table bird; white Rocks helped found the modern broiler industry. Rocks are calm, docile and easy to manage, and many hens will go broody. They feather early and handle cold winters well. They like to free range but accept a roomy run, which makes them a good first flock for families.
